2

Christmas Letters

Each student writes a letter to their family.

RecordingWeek of November 25–26

How it works

  1. Each student writes the letter. The theme is “A letter to my family”.
  2. You correct the letter with the student.
  3. Practice reading it out loud together. The reading is what we will record.
  4. Keep the letters in your folder. We recommend it and we encourage it: students lose them.

3

Christmas Houses

Each student’s house holds something special inside.

Why this matters

It makes the house personal.

Each student chooses a word and a name they want to keep safe and writes them on the inside walls. That choice is what turns a craft into their own house.

It gives them a real reason to use English.

Why this word? Who is this person? Let them think and talk about it before they write.

Nobody reads what is inside.

The house is glued shut with the word inside. That promise is what makes the choice honest, so please do not check or correct what they write.

How it works

  1. Show both houses and let each student choose one.
  2. Before anyone writes, talk about it: “What is something you want to keep safe?”
  3. Students write a word and a name on the inside walls (the back of the sheet), before gluing.
  4. Remind them that nobody reads what is inside. Do not check it or correct it.
  5. Color, cut, fold and glue. The house closes with the word inside and hangs from a string.

Files: eic-christmas-decoration.web.app. Print at 100% on 140 to 180 gsm paper, double-sided, flip on short edge.

5

Reading for Kids 1 and 2

Get to know the tool before you use it in class.

Open it here: eic-reading-tool.web.app. Choose Kids 1 or Kids 2 in the index.

What you will find

Story Time (A).

Comic stories. Each student plays a character and reads a speech bubble in turn.

Read the World (B).

A simple reading page for the second lesson of the unit.

18 readings per level.

Nine units, with an A and a B in each unit.

How to explore it

  1. Open the index and choose Kids 1 or Kids 2.
  2. Pick a unit. Start with an A, the Story Time.
  3. Try the Cast: each student plays a character, and the bubbles light up one by one.
  4. Try the Remember layer: words go missing, then the bubbles are hidden.
  5. Find the teacher notes toggle.
